On an L4 lattice, §9Unbind§r (click it twice in the Supermassive Lattice panel, as Bind and Shed also take two clicks, or OpenComputers setUnbound) lets the setpoint pass 67,108,864 SM. n = log2(M / 67,108,864) is the number of doublings past the top. Hold §9n 1 or more for 1 hour§r with the anchor paid.

§5§lTHE §lANCHOR§r Every second the hole costs§9 1,024 × 4^(n²) L§r of Primordial Matter (GT's Transcendent Plasma Mixer), from the trim sockets or the rim gas sockets (ME stocking hatches work only in the gas sockets):
- n 0.5 (94.9 M SM): 1,448 L/s
- n 1 (134 M SM):§9 4,096 L/s§r
- n 1.5 (190 M SM): 23,170 L/s
- n 2 (268 M SM): 262,144 L/s
- n 3 (537 M SM): 2.7e8 L/s, impossible
Short of it, the hole §9sheds safely§r at 2 % a second to the doubling your supply pays for (with no Primordial Matter at all, back to the L4 top). Nothing is ever destroyed. The setpoint is kept: when the anchor is paid again, the hole grows back to it; lower the setpoint to stay where it is.

The Primordial Matter on hand caps the Unbound mass: with an ME stocking hatch that is the whole network's stock, so the hole grows until the anchor burns it faster than you refill it. Set the setpoint to the doubling your supply keeps up with.

Growth: one doubling per 8.2 h on Helium at the cap; the hold-up stays 3×. Unbound adds no power (the curve is flat): it makes Overdrive cheaper.

§2§lDONE §lWHEN§r the GUI has shown n of at least 1, with the anchor fully paid, for an hour (tick the box).
